newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria proposes pegging lev to mark from July 1.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria proposes pegging lev to mark from July 1.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Minister Muravei Radev said on Tuesday the cabinet would propose pegging the lev to the mark at a fixed exchange rate of 1,000 from July 1, when a currency board system is launched.
"The cabinet will propose to use the German mark as an anchor in a currency board arrangement at a rate of 1,000 levs per mark," Radev told a news conference.
Radev said the cabinet would propose that parliament include the mark/lev peg as an article in the new central bank law due to be voted on at a final reading on Wednesday or Thursday.

Under a currency board system recommended by the International Monetary Fund to stabilise Bulgaria's economy, levs in circulation must be exactly matched by central bank issuing department foreign exchange reserves.
Bulgaria will enter the currency board arrangement with issue department reserves of around $1 billion, said IMF team leader Anne McGuirk.
Radev said this year's projected GDP is 16.15 trillion levs, in a draft budget which has to be approved by cabinet and parliament by end-June.
Assumed revenue in this year's budget was seen at 27.3 percent of GDP, expenses at 33.5 percent of GDP.
The budget deficit was assumed at 6.2 percent of GDP, higher than the IMF's recommendation of 3.8 percent due to pending interest payments on Bulgarian foreign and domestic debt.
An average lev/dollar exchange rate of 1,700 was assumed in the 1997 budget. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88 ($ = 1645 Bulgarian Levs)
